title.en: The war in Europe and North Africa
Thirty miles of a river city

text.en: Imagine a city 30 miles long along a great river, making tractors and guns, and bearing the name of the enemy leader. Hitler wanted it badly, and the fight for it became a turning point of the war.

World War II was fought on two fronts, Europe and the Asia Pacific, with the Allies against Germany and Italy in Europe and against Japan in the Asia Pacific.
It was a modern war of tanks, submarines, battleships, aircraft carriers, fighters and bombers, so it needed raw materials, factories and technical improvements, and it became an expensive, long war of attrition.
Germany used Blitzkrieg, the lightning strike, to storm into countries, taking Denmark, Norway and then France, until by 1941 all mainland Europe up to the Russian frontier was in Axis hands.
At Dunkirk in May 1940 more than 300,000 British and French soldiers were forced back to the beaches, and Britain would have struggled to regroup if so many had been lost.
In the Battle of Britain, from July 1940, Hitler tried to force Britain to accept peace by bombing ports, airfields and factories, and in September 1940 London suffered the Blitz.
The air campaign failed because radar let the Royal Air Force spot German bombers early and inflict severe losses, so the raids stopped after October 1940 and the invasion plan was dropped.
President Roosevelt could not take the United States into the war directly, so in March 1941 he began Lend Lease, sending arms, food and supplies to Britain disguised as a loan, worth 46.5 billion dollars between 1941 and 1945.
In June 1941 Germany invaded Russia to seize land for Germans, destroy the communist regime and take resources such as oil, and its army pushed 1000 miles in and marched on Moscow.
Soviet resistance and the fierce Russian winter finally stopped the German advance.
Stalingrad, an industrial city of about 30 miles along the Volga, mattered because taking it would cut Soviet transport to the south, open the Caucasus oil fields and give Hitler a propaganda victory, and Germany's plan was called Fall Blau, Operation Blue.
The Battle of Stalingrad ran from 17 July 1942 to 2 February 1943, and the Soviet people defended the city even after about 15 million civilian deaths and about 10 million soldiers killed, over a tenth of Russia's population.
In North Africa General Rommel's forces took ground quickly and left the British only Egypt, but at El Alamein in 1942 the Allies under General Montgomery defeated the Germans and Italians and chased them out.
The victory in North Africa gave the Allies a base to invade Italy, and in 1943 a new Italian government surrendered after Mussolini was thrown out.
The Germans set Mussolini up as a puppet ruler in the north, and Italian partisans killed him in April 1945.
General Eisenhower led the Allied invasion of Normandy in France, and the German army was slowly pushed back.
From 1944 the Russian army attacked from the east, capturing much of Eastern Europe and Poland, and in 1945 it occupied parts of Berlin.
Hitler committed suicide in April 1945, the war in Europe ended in May 1945, and Germany was divided into two sections.

problem.en: Why did Germany want Stalingrad, and why did it fail to take it?

text.en: Stalingrad was an industrial city on the Volga making armaments and tractors.

why.en: Capturing it would cut Soviet links to the south.

text.en: It would also open the Caucasus oil fields and give Hitler a propaganda victory over Stalin's name.

why.en: Fall Blau, Operation Blue, began on 28 June 1942 with German successes.

text.en: The Soviet people defended it fiercely, and the Russian winter helped, so the battle ended on 2 February 1943.

prompt.en: Describe how radar and Lend Lease helped Britain survive.

requiredIdeas.en: Radar allowed the RAF to inflict severe losses on German bombers
The Battle of Britain raids stopped after October 1940
Lend Lease sent arms and food to Britain as a loan worth 46.5 billion dollars

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking Lend Lease was a gift with no return
Thinking the United States entered the war in March 1941

points.en: Blitzkrieg conquered most of Europe by 1941.
Dunkirk, Battle of Britain (radar), Lend Lease.
El Alamein, Italy's surrender 1943, Normandy; Europe's war ended May 1945.
